content.title: The Men's March Madness Bracket Reveal is Happening Right Now
content.text: March Madness—aka my Roman Empire—is upon us and it all starts with Selection Sunday this weekend, when the NCAA Selection Committee will reveal the 68-team bracket for the 2026 Men's Division I Basketball Tournament. The event officially kicks off one of the most exciting stretches in all of sports. From insane buzzer beaters to wild upsets and Cinderella stories, this year is bound to be thrilling. But whether you're a die-hard college basketball fan like me (let's go St. John's!) who can't wait to see this year's seeds, or someone who just loves filling out an annual bracket with friends, here's everything you need to know about Selection Sunday.🎬 SIGN UP for Parade’s Daily newsletter to get the latest pop culture news & celebrity interviews delivered right to your inbox 🎬 When Is Selection Sunday 2026?Selection Sunday is this Sunday, March 15, 2026.AdvertisementWhat Time Does Selection Sunday Start?The men's bracket reveal begins at 6 p.m. ET. The one-hour selection show will unveil all 68 teams, their seedings and their first-round matchups. (And I'll get to see where my brother's beloved Villanova Wildcats land in the bracket after their heartbreaking Thursday night loss to Georgetown in the Big East tournament.)If you're also interested in women's March Madness, the women's bracket will be revealed later that evening at 8 p.m. ET on ESPN.Related: 'Brack to the Future' and 'Hoop, There It Is'—We've Got 75 Funny NCAA March Madness Bracket NamesWhat Channel Is Selection Sunday On?The men's Selection Sunday show airs on CBS. You can also stream it live on Paramount+ (you'll need the Premium tier) and the CBS Sports app.AdvertisementAdditional streaming options include DirecTV, YouTubeTV, Hulu + Live TV and FuboTV.How Does Selection Sunday Work?If you're new to March Madness, welcome to the most chaotic and addictive event in sports. Here's how it works: The NCAA Tournament features 68 teams. Thirty-one of those spots go to teams that win their conference tournaments—those are called automatic bids. The remaining 37 spots are called "at-large" bids. These are hand-picked by the NCAA Selection Committee based on each team's performance throughout the season.During Selection Sunday, the committee reveals the full bracket. This is when we know which teams made the cut, their seedings (ranked 1 through 16 in four different regions of the country) and their first-round matchups. The seedings matter because they determine who plays who: a No. 1 seed faces a No. 16 seed, a No. 2 plays a No. 15 and so on. So when a team gets an unexpectedly high seed in the double digits, they are going to play an excellent team during the first round.AdvertisementBut the real drama comes into play with the "bubble teams"—the ones right on the edge of making it in. In 2023, North Carolina became the first AP pre-season No. 1 team to miss the tournament entirely since the field expanded in 1985. Their head coach—Hubert Davis—was asked if he had a pitch for why his team deserved a bid. His response? "At the end of the day, we had our chances." Savage!Think of Selection Sunday like the final rose on The Bachelor—except instead of roses it's a ticket to the Big Dance—and instead of one person crying, it's entire college campuses. Every year, there are tears of joy, tears of heartbreak and a whole lot of screaming at the TV. And that's before the tournament even kicks off!Michigan's Yaxel Lendeborg dunks the ball against Ohio State during the quarterfinals of the 2026 Big Ten Men's Basketball Tournament. The Wolverines are expected to get the No. 1 seed in the NCAA tournament on Selection Sunday.Michael Reeves/Getty Images (Michael Reeves/Getty Images)Which Teams Are Expected to Be No. 1 Seeds?Based on the latest bracket projections, the four projected No. 1 seeds heading into Selection Sunday are:AdvertisementDuke Blue DevilsMichigan WolverinesArizona WildcatsFlorida GatorsRelated: 45 March Madness Trivia Questions and Answers To Test Your KnowledgeWhat Is the Full 2026 Men's NCAA Tournament Schedule?Here's the complete schedule from Selection Sunday through the National Championship:Selection Sunday: Sunday, March 15 — 6 p.m. ET on CBSFirst Four: Tuesday, March 17 and Wednesday, March 18 — Dayton, OhioFirst Round: Thursday, March 19 and Friday, March 20Second Round:Saturday, March 21 and Sunday, March 22Sweet 16: Thursday, March 26 and Friday, March 27Elite Eight: Saturday, March 28 and Sunday, March 29Final Four: Saturday, April 4 — Lucas Oil Stadium, IndianapolisNational Championship: Monday, April 6 — Lucas Oil Stadium, IndianapolisWhere to Watch March Madness Games After Selection SundayOnce the tournament begins, games will be broadcast across CBS, TBS, TNT and truTV. Note that CBS games will also stream on Paramount+ and you can watch the TBS, TNT and truTV games on HBO Max. All 67 games will be available on NCAA March Madness Live (online and via the app).If you have a live TV streaming subscription, DirecTV, YouTubeTV, Hulu + Live TV and FuboTV carry all four networks.AdvertisementHow Can I Fill Out or Print a Bracket?After the bracket is revealed on Sunday night, you can fill out your bracket on ESPN.com, CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports and NCAA.com—all of which offer free bracket challenge games and printable versions. It's one of the most fun annual traditions in sports, even if you don't follow college basketball closely. President Obama famously does it every year and you can even play against him!Next, Sister Jean, Beloved March Madness Icon and Loyola Legend, Dies at 106 This story was originally published by Parade on Mar 14, 2026, where it first appeared in the TV section.
